post.description: OAuth2 password flow, so the Swagger UI 'Authorize' button works.
Bulk onboarding. Upserts by camera_code; bad rows are reported, not fatal.

API onboarding: read someone else's camera catalogue and register every camera.

`url` may be the catalogue endpoint itself or just the host — the documented sandbox
path (`/api/ingest`) and the other usual ones are tried in turn. Field names are mapped
tolerantly (see catalogue.py): departments by code, seeded name or hint, coordinates in
most shapes (checked against a Gujarat box), districts by name or spelling variant or
from the coordinates. A record we cannot map is reported instead of failing the batch, and
every guess is kept as a warning in the camera's tags.

analytics: anpr (default) runs the analytics worker where the catalogue marks the camera
ANPR-viable or explicitly asks for analytics (e.g. counts on a wide camera) · all runs it
everywhere · none registers cameras for viewing only.
dry_run: write nothing; the response adds `rows`, each camera as it would be registered
(department, district, lat/lon, where the coordinates came from, warnings), so the
mapping can be checked first.

get.description:
Vehicle and person counts from the analytics workers.

Each stored row is one camera x one window: frames analysed plus detections per class.
A detection is a box in one frame, not a unique vehicle or person, so the figures that
mean something are per analysed frame: `in_view` (average number in frame) and `peak`
(most in any single frame). Both are independent of the sampling rate. Raw `detections`
are returned for completeness and are frame-detections, not a count of vehicles.
Aggregates only: no per-detection listing exists, and none is exposed.
Window: `since`/`until` when given, else the last `hours`.
Coverage gap analysis: where the network is thin, blind, or offline.

post.description:
Non-plate detections. Workers send `object_counts`: one row per camera per window,
value = frames analysed, detail = detections and peak per class. Other event types
(crowd density, loitering, ...) use the same path.

get.description:
Cameras an analytics worker may consume: analytics enabled and a stream URL present.
RTSP is preferred; a camera a catalogue lists with HLS only is read over HLS instead.

The edge copy of the active vehicle watchlist, so a worker cut off from the API can
still flag a hit locally. Only what matching needs: no names, reasons or case refs.
